description: Case C2: the planner records the same facts under off-vocabulary key names, so the required facts read as missing; the harness must flag it loudly, preserve the keys unchanged, and never guess a mapping.
why_it_exists: Observed on MAT-20260102-006: own_vehicle_registration was reported missing while registration = "9XYZ876" sat in the same facts object, plus incident_datetime missing beside incident_date + incident_time, and damage_description missing beside damage. Validate Plan JSON marks a required fact missing with hasOwnProperty(facts, rf), and the planner had written the value under a key of its own choosing. The prompt's rule 11 forbade inventing key names, but rule 11 lived only in the prompt.

input.facts_json: {"incident_description": "Rear quarter panel struck while the vehicle was parked and unattended.", "incident_location": "Level 2, Hay Street car park, Perth WA", "owner_present": "no", "driver_identity": "vehicle was unattended", "registration": "9XYZ876", "incident_date": "2026-08-14", "incident_time": "09:20", "damage": "Dent and paint transfer to the rear quarter panel."}

items.facts_json: {"incident_description": "Rear quarter panel struck while the vehicle was parked and unattended.", "incident_location": "Level 2, Hay Street car park, Perth WA", "owner_present": "no", "driver_identity": "vehicle was unattended", "registration": "9XYZ876", "incident_date": "2026-08-14", "incident_time": "09:20", "damage": "Dent and paint transfer to the rear quarter panel."}

expect.unmapped_facts_json: {"registration": "9XYZ876", "incident_date": "2026-08-14", "incident_time": "09:20", "damage": "Dent and paint transfer to the rear quarter panel."}

assertions: NO MAPPING: registration is not silently bound to own_vehicle_registration - nothing in the record says whether 9XYZ876 is the owner's vehicle or another party's, and binding a guessed value to a legal fact is worse than reporting the gap.
NOTHING IS DISCARDED: every off-vocabulary key stays in facts_json under its original name; unmapped_facts_json is an audit copy, not a relocation.
Any off-vocabulary key with a real value raises UNKNOWN_FACT_KEYS and sets requires_human_review.
An off-vocabulary key coexisting with a missing REQUIRED fact additionally raises REQUIRED_FACT_MAY_BE_MISKEYED - that combination is the one that produced the false gap.

Keys the pipeline itself injects (matter_id, route, is_new_matter, dry_run, test_data_only, force_proceed, owner_chat_id, jurisdiction) are control values, not claims about the matter, and are never counted as off-vocabulary.
A key whose value is blank or a placeholder (UNKNOWN, MISSING, UNOBTAINABLE, N/A, NA, NONE, TBC, TBD, PENDING) is not counted as an unmapped fact.
The owner summary states the unmapped key names and explicitly declines to say which is which.
